title: Retention-tier pricing pilot + subprocessor attestation for EU/UK enterprise contracts
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Run a controlled pricing and contract experiment that introduces retention-based pricing tiers for enterprise customers in EU/UK, combined with an upstream subprocessor attestation pack and SCC-compliant template language. Goal: surface whether explicit retention SLAs + subprocessor transparency materially increase willingness to pay and shorten procurement cycles for regulated customers.
hypothesis: Offering a lower-priced tier with strict 7/30/90-day retention options and an auditable subprocessor attestation reduces procurement friction for mid-enterprise customers in EU/UK, increasing conversion to Dedicated/Private by 10% within pilot cohort and decreasing average contract negotiation time by 20%.
success_metrics:
1) Conversion lift to Dedicated/Private from pilot cohort >= 10%
2) Average procurement cycle reduction >= 20%
3) Percentage of pilot customers selecting non-default retention tier >= 30%
4) No measurable regression on unit economics > 8%
assumptions:
1) Legal & security can produce an attestation pack within 2 cycles.
2) Engineering can implement enforcement + billing for retention tiers with a gated rollout.
3) SCCs template is acceptable to legal counsels in target customers or can be negotiated without counterparty changes.
out_of_scope: Full productization of retention UI for self-serve customers and changes to default Hosted API retention policies beyond the pilot cohort.
work_items: Draft contract addendum (legal) with configurable retention clauses and SCCs references
Create subprocessor attestation document summarizing list + contractual commitments
Billing changes: map retention option to discount bands and reporting in Console
Implement retention-enforcement controls in Dedicated/Private deploy flows for pilot customers
Onboarding playbook for Solutions & Sales including negotiation playbook and FAQ
dependencies: ENG-4872 (billing platform: discount dimension for retention tiers)
ENG-4933 (data lifecycle enforcement + retention delete job)
acceptance_criteria:
1) Legal sign-off on contract addendum and SCCs language for pilot customers.
2) Engineering deploys retention enforcement for one Dedicated customer and verifies deletion within SLA in test harness.
3) Billing records retention selections and applies discount band on invoice preview.
4) Sales completes at least three signed proof-of-concept pilot agreements using the new addendum.
notes: Design will produce a minimal console flow showing retention selection during Dedicated onboarding; full UI polish deferred post-experiment. Coordinate with Privacy Ops to ensure audit trail for deletions. Consider a short-term data processor-level SLA addendum for high-risk customers.
updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with Legal, Security, Eng, Sales. Agreed scope and timeline. Action: Legal to draft addendum by 2025-02-21.
2025-02-21: Legal draft complete (link above). Security requested additional attestation fields for subprocessors (encryption-at-rest, location controls). Added to work_items.
2025-02-26: ENG-4933 assigned to Priya Rao. Estimate revised after review (requires a retention enforcement microservice + test harness).
2025-03-01: Sales recruited 5 potential pilot customers in EU/UK (financial services, healthcare SaaS). Outreach underway. Expect 2 signed by mid-March.
2025-03-03: Internal review with Finance; preliminary model shows ~6% unit economics impact at 15% adoption of discounted tier — within tolerance. Proceeding with pilot.
review_feedback: Legal: prefer a single addendum referencing SCCs + retention schedule rather than per-customer redlines to speed negotiations.
Security: require KMS boundary statement and minimum encryption controls in attestation pack.
Engineering: propose an initial soft-enforcement mode (flag + monitoring) before hard deletes to reduce risk during pilot.
next_steps: Legal to finalize addendum and produce a one-page customer summary (due 2025-03-07)
Engineering to deliver soft-enforcement telemetry and billing integration for retention selection (target 2025-03-14)
Sales to close first two pilot contracts and collect negotiation time feedback (target 2025-03-20)
Privacy Ops to run a tabletop incident scenario to validate deletion proofing (target 2025-03-17)
